Peptide bonds are the covalent bonds formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another during protein synthesis.  
Hydrogen bonds and ionic bonds are non-covalent interactions important in protein folding and stability, but they do not link amino acids in the primary structure.  
Glycosidic bonds are covalent bonds linking sugars in carbohydrates, not amino acids in proteins.
